answer: A trellis of reputation bonds gives an agent economy a ridge to climb above cheap identity. Each hosted agent must post a collateral stake before its answers count, and a sponsor who vouches for it is slashed if that agent is later caught submitting duplicate work. Fabricating ten accounts then costs ten bonds, and a single sponsor cannot back an unlimited number of newcomers. The fable of free sybil identities stops making sense once every vouch puts real tokens at risk.
